correctness.rationale: Direct Gaussian moment integration yields the normalized Wigner expression; the closest momentum fringe begins at t=(pi-arccos(exp(-a^2)))/(2a). Other fringes are suppressed by a Gaussian tail at t+pi/a. In first-fringe coordinates v=2t(p-t), w=sqrt(2t)q, the rescaled negative part tends to (sqrt(2)v-w^2)_+ and is dominated by an integrable exp(-v)v indicator of |w|<=C sqrt(v). Its exact Gamma(5/2) integral gives the factor 2^(-3/4)/sqrt(pi) in front of a^2 t^(-5/2) exp(-t^2); the edge expansion gives the stated 2^(7/4)exp(-1/2)/pi^3 coefficient and both exponent scales. The packaged checker directly recomputes three Wigner defining integrals and four first-fringe ratios. Remote-fringe and infinite-parameter results are proved, not inferred from experiments.

originality.rationale: The underlying even-cat Wigner distribution and negativity invariant are already present in the 2004 Kenfack–Życzkowski paper and are not claimed to be original. Its inspected Section III has numerical studies and an upper approximation, not an exact small-packet-separation asymptotic of the integrated negative part. The 2013 primary cat-state fidelity paper does not imply a negative-volume equivalent. The closest prior local Wigner two-Hermite claim concerns an exact two-dimensional Hermite span, not the nonpolynomial Gaussian cat; its near-vacuum rate is not transferable to all infinitely many Hermite amplitudes. published-finding corpus queries returned no identical or stronger small-separation cat mass law. The asymptotic equivalent, with a fractional power and two essential-exponential scales, survives comparison, with explicit unindexed-literature priority risk.

value.rationale: The integrated negative Wigner volume is a canonical quantitative nonclassicality invariant explicitly studied for Gaussian cats in a major 2004 paper. The exact near-vacuum rate was not supplied by its established Wigner formula or numerical plots. The result computes a genuinely nonperturbative tail: the first negative interference fringe migrates to momentum pi/(2a) while a transverse boundary layer collapses. The full equivalent identifies a fractional-power prefactor, dominant 1/a^2 rate, distinct 1/a correction, and leading constant. This distinguishes the exact infinite coherent superposition from any simple finite-order wavefunction approximation, quantifies detectability at small separation, and is meaningful without a downstream theorem.
